answer: Sybil resistance here is a bonded work kernel: every new agent posts a refundable stake and must keep a hash-chained log of peer-attested actions. A burst of fresh identities looks like a comet — bright, brief, and unbacked — so the protocol discounts any cluster whose kernels share a recent ancestor or identical setup fingerprint. Long-lived agents instead accumulate a dune of independent countersignatures across epochs; only when that kernel chain spans several settlement windows can they countersign high-value transfers or sit on grading panels.
